mainTopic: Whether a public well of עולי בבל is shared or ownerless, whether רב נחמן holds of בְּרֵירָה, and a new משנה that produce follows its owner's תחום.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a משנה from מסכת נדרים. Two people who forbade each other with a vow may still use public property of עולי בבל, like a well in the middle of the road, but not property of their own city. רבא uses this to challenge רב נחמן: if a public well were shared by all Jews, another משנה says partners under such a vow may not wash in their shared well. The first answer is that washing is forbidden but drawing water is allowed, because each person draws only from his own share. The גמרא then objects that this answer needs בְּרֵירָה. It shows from a משנה about brothers who are partners, as explained by רב ענן, that רב נחמן rejects בְּרֵירָה even when brothers split their animals evenly. So the גמרא gives a new explanation: everyone agrees the public well is ownerless, and the dispute is whether picking up a found object for a friend makes the friend the owner. Finally, a new משנה teaches that produce in another city follows its owner's תחום. Others may bring it to him only if he himself made an עירוב that reaches it.

steps.title: The vow rules: both forbidden to each other, but public property of עולי בבל is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues. If two people forbid themselves to each other, they may not benefit from one another. They may still use things belonging to עולי בבל, but not things belonging to their own city.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'You are a חרם to me,' the one who made the vow is forbidden. If he says 'I am forbidden to you and you to me,' both are forbidden to each other. They may still use things belonging to עולי בבל, but not things belonging to that city.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing to quote a משנה from נדרים that רבא is using as his source. It is laying the groundwork for the challenge that comes in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two kinds of public property are set apart here. Things of עולי בבל belong to no particular owner, so neither person benefits from the other's share. Things of 'that city' are owned by the townspeople, so each of the two owns a piece, and using them means benefiting from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow that makes something forbidden, like something dedicated
The one who made the vow
Those who came up from Babylonia; used here to mean public property of the whole Jewish people
That city; property owned jointly by the people of the town

phrases.english: [If he said:] 'You are hereby forbidden to me as a חרם' —
the one who made the vow is forbidden.
[If he said:] 'I am forbidden to you, and you to me' —
both of them are forbidden to benefit from each other,
and they are permitted to use the things of those who came up from Babylonia,
but they are forbidden to use the things of that city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the משנה in נדרים that רבא began citing before this section.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a public well of עולי בבל counts as shared property
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת נדרים about two people who made a vow against each other

steps.title: Examples: what counts as property of עולי בבל and what belongs to the city
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists examples. Property of עולי בבל includes הר הבית, the chambers, the courtyards, and a well in the middle of the road. City property includes the street, the בית הכנסת, and the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are things of עולי בבל: הר הבית, the chambers, the courtyards, and a well in the middle of the road. These are things of that city: the street, the בית הכנסת, and the bathhouse.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives concrete examples of each type of property. The key detail for the coming challenge is that a well in the middle of the road counts as property of עולי בבל, which the vow does not forbid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'well in the middle of the road' is what רבא needs. The משנה says the two people may use it. רבא will ask how that fits with the idea that such a well belongs to everyone as partners.

keyTerms.meaning: Chambers or rooms on the Temple Mount

steps.confusionAlert: Don't skip the well in the middle of the road as just one more example. The whole challenge in the next step is built on it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן דְּבָרִים שֶׁל עוֹלֵי בָבֶל:
phrases.english: And these are the things of those who came up from Babylonia:
the Temple Mount, the chambers, and the courtyards,
and a well in the middle of the road.
And these are the things of that city:
the street, the synagogue, and the bathhouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן דְּבָרִים שֶׁל עוֹלֵי בָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quoted משנה by giving examples of the two categories named in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: Status of a public well in the middle of the road
steps.raayaSupportSource: The examples listed in the משנה in נדרים

steps.title: If a public well is shared property, why may the two people use it?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן. If a public well belongs to everyone as partners, it should be forbidden, since another משנה says partners under such a vow may not enter their shared courtyard to wash in its well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say a public well belongs to partners, why is it permitted? Didn't we learn in a משנה that partners who vowed not to benefit from each other may not enter the courtyard to wash in the well?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now delivers his challenge. The first משנה allows the two people to use a public well, but if that well were shared property, a second משנה says they would be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן treats a public well as owned jointly by all Jews. If so, both people under the vow own a share, just like partners in a courtyard. The משנה about partners forbids them to wash in their shared well, so the public well should be forbidden too. Yet the first משנה permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Aramaic for a well (the same as בּוֹר)
But didn't we learn in a משנה?

phrases.english: And if you say a [public] well belongs to partners,
why is it permitted [for the two people under the vow]?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: הַשּׁוּתָּפִין שֶׁנָּדְרוּ הֲנָאָה זֶה מִזֶּה —
phrases.english: But didn't we learn: partners who vowed not to benefit from each other —
are forbidden to enter the [shared] courtyard
to wash in the well!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ בֵּירָא דְשׁוּתָּפֵי הוּא, אַמַּאי מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the quoted משנה (steps 1-2) and sets it against a second משנה to attack רב נחמן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that a public well of עולי בבל is owned jointly by everyone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Partners under a vow may not use their shared well (משנה in נדרים). If a public well is shared, it should be forbidden, yet the משנה permits it.

steps.title: Washing is forbidden, but drawing water is allowed because each draws from his own share
steps.stepSummary: The answer agrees that washing in a shared well is forbidden. The משנה that permits the public well is talking about filling water, where each person counts as drawing only from his own share.
steps.simpleTranslation: For washing, that is indeed so. But what case are we dealing with here? Drawing water. This one draws from his own share, and that one draws from his own share.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge by splitting the two cases: washing versus drawing water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person washes in the well, he uses all of its water, including the other partner's part, so it is forbidden. When he draws water, the water he takes counts as coming only from his own share. So the vow is not broken, and רב נחמן's view that the well is shared still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, that is so (agreeing with part of the challenge)
What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow the case)

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the answer separates washing, which is forbidden because you use all the water, from drawing water, which is allowed because each one draws from his own share. Steps 5-7 knock this answer down, and step 8 replaces it.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the public well isn't shared. It agrees the well is shared and explains why drawing from it is still allowed.

phrases.english: To wash, indeed it is so [forbidden],
but with what are we dealing here? With filling [water],
this one fills from his own [share],
and that one fills from his own [share].

steps.triggerLanguage: לִרְחוֹץ הָכִי נָמֵי, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 3 by narrowing the case to drawing water.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: separating washing from drawing water
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any use of a shared well by partners under a vow is forbidden, so a public, shared well should be forbidden too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only washing, which uses all the water, is forbidden. Drawing water is allowed because each person counts as taking from his own share.

steps.title: Does רב נחמן really hold of retroactive designation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רב נחמן holds of בְּרֵירָה. It quotes a משנה about brothers who are partners: when they owe the קלבון they are exempt from מעשר בהמה, and when they owe מעשר בהמה they are exempt from the קלבון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רב נחמן really hold that there is בְּרֵירָה? But we learned in a משנה: brothers who are partners, when they must pay the קלבון, are exempt from מעשר בהמה. And when they must give מעשר בהמה, they are exempt from the קלבון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a challenge. It asks whether רב נחמן really holds of בְּרֵירָה, and it brings a משנה that will be used against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 4 said each person filling from the well takes only his own share. That only works if we say בְּרֵירָה: looking back, this water was always his. The משנה shows that brothers can count either as partners or as one inheritance, and which one they are changes their obligations.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: deciding now that a portion was always someone's from the start
But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a source used to challenge)
A small extra coin added to the yearly half-שקל given to the בית המקדש
The tithe of animals: every tenth animal born in the herd is set aside

steps.confusionAlert: The two rules are opposites. Partners pay the קלבון but are exempt from מעשר בהמה. One undivided inheritance gives מעשר בהמה but is exempt from the קלבון. A group of brothers is always in one situation or the other, never both.

phrases.english: And does Rav Nachman hold that there is retroactive designation?
phrases.notes: This points back to Step 4, where each person drawing water counts as taking only from his own share.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
Brothers who are partners,
phrases.notes: These are brothers who divided their inheritance and then joined their property together again.

phrases.english: when they are obligated in the kalbon,
they are exempt from the animal tithe.
And when they are obligated in the animal tithe,
phrases.notes: This is when the brothers have not divided yet, so everything still counts as one inheritance.

phrases.english: they are exempt from the kalbon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַב נַחְמָן יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the idea behind Step 4's answer, that each person draws from his own share, by asking whether רב נחמן holds of בְּרֵירָה at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that רב נחמן holds יש בְּרֵירָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה, together with how it is explained, will show how inherited property is treated after it is divided. This will be used to test whether רב נחמן accepts בְּרֵירָה.

steps.title: רב ענן limits the משנה to dividing kids against lambs
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן explains that the משנה treats the brothers as new partners only if they split the animals unevenly by type, kids for lambs. If each took kids from the kids and lambs from the lambs, we say each share was his from the very beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ענן said: The משנה only taught this when they divided kids against lambs and lambs against kids. But if they divided kids against kids and lambs against lambs, we say: this is his share, which came to him from the very first moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב ענן's explanation of the משנה, and this explanation uses בְּרֵירָה. It is setting up the next move, where this view will be compared with רב נחמן's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trading kids for lambs is like a purchase, so when the brothers join again they are brand-new partners. Splitting each type evenly is different. Using בְּרֵירָה, each brother's share counts as his own from the moment of the father's death. So if they join again, it counts as the original inheritance once more.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this when... (limits a source to a specific case)
From the very first moment, here meaning the father's death

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a clear case of בְּרֵירָה in action: looking back and saying a share was always his. It will be the test case for whether רב נחמן accepts בְּרֵירָה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב עָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: And Rav Anan said: They taught this only
when they divided kids against lambs
and lambs against kids.
But if they divided kids against kids
and lambs against lambs,
one says: This is his portion
that was due to reach him from the first moment.
phrases.notes: This is בְּרֵירָה: looking back, this share was always his from when the father died.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב עָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה from Step 5 and shows that it is read with בְּרֵירָה in mind, which builds up the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: How the משנה about brothers who are partners should be understood with respect to בְּרֵירָה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ענן's limiting explanation of the משנה

steps.title: רב נחמן rejects retroactive shares even in an even split
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says that even when brothers split kids for kids and lambs for lambs, we do not say each share was his from the beginning. So he does not hold of בְּרֵירָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב נחמן said: Even if they split kids against kids and lambs against lambs, we do not say that this share was the one coming to him from the very start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge from step 5. It quotes רב נחמן himself saying he does not accept בְּרֵירָה at all, even in the easiest case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רב ענן said an even split (kids for kids, lambs for lambs) counts as if each brother owned his share from the start. רב נחמן disagrees even in that case. So the answer in step 4, that each person draws only from his own share of a partnership well, cannot fit רב נחמן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: deciding now that something was yours from the beginning

steps.confusionAlert: The quote does not prove that the well is forbidden. It only proves that רב נחמן cannot use the 'own share' answer from step 4. The גמרא will now need a new explanation.

phrases.english: But רב נחמן said:
Even if they divided kids against kids
and lambs against lambs
one does not say: this is his portion
that was coming to him from the first moment.
phrases.notes: This is the even split that רב ענן accepted in step 6. רב נחמן rejects even that.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חָלְקוּ גְּדָיִם כְּנֶגֶד גְּדָיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in step 5. It quotes רב נחמן disagreeing with רב ענן (step 6) and rejecting בְּרֵירָה even in an even split. This undoes the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 4 that, for רב נחמן, filling from a partnership well counts as taking from one's own share.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That answer depends on בְּרֵירָה. רב נחמן rejects בְּרֵירָה even in an even split, so the answer cannot be his.

steps.title: New explanation: the dispute is about acquiring a found object for a friend
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the partnership approach. Everyone agrees the public well is ownerless. The dispute is whether picking up a found item for a friend makes the friend the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees that a public well is ownerless. Here they disagree about someone who picks up a found item for his friend. One master holds the friend acquires it, and one master holds the friend does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a completely new explanation of the argument about water from the public well. It moves the dispute away from partnership and into the laws of acquiring a found object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the well is ownerless (הֶפְקֵר), it belongs to no one, so there is no partnership and no need for בְּרֵירָה. Drawn water is like a found object. If drawing it for a friend makes the friend the owner, the water follows the friend's תחום. If not, it belongs to the one who drew it and follows his תחום.

keyTerms.meaning: Picking up a found object on behalf of a friend

steps.whatToRemember: A public well belongs to no one. The argument is whether picking up a found item for your friend makes it his. That decides whose תחום the water follows.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the whole partnership problem. רב נחמן's position now rests on acquiring for someone else, not on בְּרֵירָה.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees
it is an ownerless well,
phrases.notes: This is the well of עולי בבל from the משנה, the public well in the middle of the road.

phrases.english: but here
they disagree about one who picks up a found object for his friend.
One master holds: he acquires,
phrases.notes: The friend becomes the owner, so the water follows the friend's תחום. This fits רב נחמן.

phrases.english: and one master holds: he does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בֵּירָא דְהֶפְקֵרָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the partnership explanation that step 7 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-framing the dispute: from partnership and בְּרֵירָה to acquiring a found object for someone else
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the public well was a partnership, so רב נחמן needed בְּרֵירָה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The well is ownerless. The dispute is whether picking up a found object for a friend gives the friend ownership.

steps.title: New משנה: produce kept in another city
steps.stepSummary: If a person's produce is in another city, the people there may not bring it to him on יום טוב, even if they made an עירוב. If he made an עירוב himself, his produce is treated like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone's produce was in another city, and the people of that city made an עירוב to bring him some of it, they may not bring it to him. But if he made an עירוב, his produce is like him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that produce can move only as far as its owner may walk, even if other people are carrying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things follow their owner's תחום. The townspeople's own עירוב does not help, because the produce is limited to where its owner may go. If the owner made an עירוב that lets him reach that city, the produce gets the same range and may be brought to him.

keyTerms.meaning: An arrangement that extends how far one may walk on שבת or יום טוב
Like him, meaning it has the same walking limits as its owner

steps.confusionAlert: The townspeople's עירוב is not enough. What matters is the owner's limit, because the produce is 'like his feet.'

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One whose produce was in another city
and the people of that city made an עירוב
to bring him some of his produce
they may not bring it to him.
But if he made an עירוב
his produce is like him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It continues the theme that objects follow their owner's תחום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce follows its owner's תחום. Others may bring it to him only if he himself made an עירוב that reaches it.
